title: Loops + Decisions
summary: Combine for loops with if/else — so each step of the loop can make its own choice.

content.title: Checking Inside Every Step
content.summary: An if statement inside a loop runs a check on every single iteration.
content.body:
You can put an if statement inside a loop. Python checks the condition every time the loop runs:

for i in range(5):
    if i == 2:
        print("Treasure!")
    else:
        print("Empty room...")

Output:
Empty room...
Empty room...
Treasure!
Empty room...
Empty room...

The loop runs 5 times. On step 2 it finds treasure; all other steps find nothing.

content.title: Even and Odd
content.summary: The % operator gives the remainder after dividing — useful for detecting every other step.

content.title: The Danger Zone
content.summary: Mark a specific loop step as special using if i == number.
content.body:
You can mark specific loop steps as special:

for i in range(1, 6):
    if i == 3:
        print("Warning! Danger zone!")
    else:
        print("Room", i, "— safe.")

Output:
Room 1 — safe.
Room 2 — safe.
Warning! Danger zone!
Room 4 — safe.
Room 5 — safe.

Each room gets checked. Only room 3 triggers the warning.

content.title: Indentation Stacks Up
content.summary: Loop body is 4 spaces in. Code inside if/else inside the loop is 8 spaces in.
content.body:
When you nest if inside a loop, both need proper indentation:

for i in range(3):         <- loop line
    if i == 1:             <- if (4 spaces in)
        print("special")  <- if-body (8 spaces in)
    else:
        print("normal")   <- else-body (8 spaces in)

The loop body is at 4 spaces. The if/else bodies are at 8 spaces.

editorPrompt: Simulate a dungeon run: loop through 6 rooms. If the room number is 4, print "Boss fight!". Otherwise, print "Room X — clear." (use i for X).
starterCode:
# Walk through 6 dungeon rooms
# Room 4 has the boss!
progressiveHints: Use for i in range(1, 7): so rooms are numbered 1 through 6.
Inside the loop, write if i == 4: then print the boss message.
Add an else: that prints "Room", i, "— clear."
challenge: Add a second special room: if the room number is 2, print a "Hidden chest!" message. You will need elif to handle two special rooms.
